---
title: "SQL Meta Command Tests"
format: live-html
---

This document tests psql-style meta commands in the SQL extension, including table listing, column inspection, role listing, environment isolation, and autocomplete for meta commands.

---

## Test 1: Table Listing

This test verifies that `\dt` lists all tables in the current PGlite environment.

```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS meta_table_a;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS meta_table_b;

CREATE TABLE meta_table_a (id INTEGER, label TEXT);
CREATE TABLE meta_table_b (id INTEGER, value NUMERIC);

INSERT INTO meta_table_a VALUES (1, 'row a');
INSERT INTO meta_table_b VALUES (1, 42.0);
```

```{sql}
#| edit: true
\dt
```

Expected result: The output lists `meta_table_a` and `meta_table_b` as available tables in the current environment.

---

## Test 2: Column Inspection

This test verifies that `\d tablename` shows the column names and data types of a specific table.

```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS meta_columns_test;

CREATE TABLE meta_columns_test (
  id       INTEGER,
  name     TEXT,
  score    NUMERIC,
  active   BOOLEAN
);
```

```{sql}
#| edit: true
\d meta_columns_test
```

Expected result: The output shows Table "public.meta_columns_test". Column details are returned as formatted text by psql-describe but are not fully rendered in tabular form by the SQL evaluator's normalizeDescribeOutput function.

---

## Test 3: Role Listing

This test verifies that `\du` lists the available database roles in the current PGlite instance.

```{sql}
#| edit: true
\du
```

Expected result: The output lists the available database roles. Since PGlite runs as a single-user in-browser database, typically only one role is shown.

---

## Test 4: Environment Isolation of Meta Commands

This test verifies that `\dt` in one exercise environment does not show tables from a different exercise environment.

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_a
#| envir: meta_env_a
#| setup: true

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS table_only_in_a;

CREATE TABLE table_only_in_a (
  id INTEGER
);

INSERT INTO table_only_in_a VALUES (1);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_a
#| envir: meta_env_a

\dt
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_b
#| envir: meta_env_b
#| setup: true

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS table_only_in_b;

CREATE TABLE table_only_in_b (
  id INTEGER
);

INSERT INTO table_only_in_b VALUES (1);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_b
#| envir: meta_env_b

\dt
```

Expected result: The `\dt` output in `ex_meta_a` shows only `table_only_in_a`. The `\dt` output in `ex_meta_b` shows only `table_only_in_b`. Tables from different environments do not appear in each other's listings.

---

## Test 5: Meta Commands in the Global Environment

This test verifies that `\dt` in a global SQL block shows only tables created in the global environment, not tables from exercise environments.

```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS global_meta_table;

CREATE TABLE global_meta_table (
  id INTEGER,
  label TEXT
);

INSERT INTO global_meta_table VALUES (1, 'global row');
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_global_check
#| setup: true

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS exercise_meta_table;

CREATE TABLE exercise_meta_table (
  id INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: ex_meta_global_check

\dt
```

```{sql}
#| edit: true

\dt
```

Expected result: The `\dt` in the exercise block shows only `exercise_meta_table`. The `\dt` in the global block shows all global available tables. Tables from exercises are not visible in the global environment and vice versa.

---

## Test 6: Invalid Meta Command Handling

This test verifies that an invalid meta command produces a meaningful error message rather than crashing the page.

```{sql}
#| edit: true
\invalidcommand
```

Expected result: The block produces an error message indicating that the meta command is not recognized. The page remains functional.

---

## Test 7: Meta Command Autocomplete

This test verifies that the SQL editor suggests available meta commands when the user types a backslash.

```{sql}
#| edit: true

-- Type "\" to verify that meta command suggestions appear,
-- including \dt, \d, \du and other supported commands.
-- before executing please delete all comments in the editor.
\dt
```

Expected result: When typing `\` in the editor, the autocomplete suggests available meta commands such as `\dt`, `\d`, `\du`. This confirms that meta commands are registered as a separate autocomplete group alongside schema-based suggestions.
